# linux_systemd_unit (Resource)

Manages the state of a systemd unit: whether it is enabled, running or masked. Attributes left unset are not managed. Use `triggers` to restart the unit when its configuration changes.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "linux_file" "app_unit" {
  path    = "/etc/systemd/system/app.service"
  content = <<-EOT
    [Unit]
    Description=My application

    [Service]
    ExecStart=/opt/app/bin/app
    Restart=on-failure

    [Install]
    WantedBy=multi-user.target
  EOT
}

resource "linux_systemd_unit" "app" {
  name          = "app.service"
  enabled       = true
  active        = true
  daemon_reload = true

  # Restart the service when its unit file changes.
  triggers = {
    unit = linux_file.app_unit.sha256
  }
}

# Reload nginx when its configuration changes.
resource "linux_systemd_unit" "nginx" {
  name           = "nginx.service"
  enabled        = true
  active         = true
  trigger_action = "reload"

  triggers = {
    config = linux_file.nginx_site.sha256
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the unit, such as `nginx.service`. Without a suffix, systemd assumes `.service`.

### Optional

- `active` (Boolean) Whether the unit is running (`systemctl start`/`stop`).
- `daemon_reload` (Boolean) Run `systemctl daemon-reload` before changing the unit, to pick up changed unit files. Defaults to `false`.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the unit starts at boot (`systemctl enable`/`disable`).
- `masked` (Boolean) Whether the unit is masked, which prevents it from starting at all (`systemctl mask`/`unmask`).
- `revert_on_destroy` (Boolean) On destroy, stop, disable and unmask the unit as far as this resource started, enabled or masked it. Otherwise destroying leaves the unit as it is. Defaults to `false`.
- `trigger_action` (String) systemctl command run when `triggers` change: `restart`, `reload`, `reload-or-restart`, `try-restart` or `try-reload-or-restart`. Defaults to `restart`.
- `triggers` (Map of String) Arbitrary values that run `trigger_action` on the unit when they change, unless the unit is stopped. For instance `{ config = linux_file.config.sha256 }`. When the resource is created with triggers, the action runs if the unit was already running.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Name of the unit.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The ID is the name of the unit.
terraform import linux_systemd_unit.nginx nginx.service
```
